messages:
ian-cs: Heads up — AcmeCorp reporting 503s starting ~08:03 UTC. They see gateway errors on hosted inference. Customer dashboard shows a spike in upstream worker crashes.
oncall-juli: on it. can you paste the first failed request id / any logs you have from CS? also what region?
ian-cs: Request ids: r=acme/req/0a1b2c3d, r=acme/req/0a1b2c3e. Region: us-west-2. They started after a batch of long-context requests (~30k tokens) from their integration.
maria-infra: attaching quick scrub of node logs (excerpt):
```
[2023-11-01T08:03:12Z] infer-runner[pid=4211]: cuda: out of memory while allocating 2147483648 bytes
[2023-11-01T08:03:12Z] infer-runner[pid=4211]: segfault at 0 ip 0x7f8a3b4c sp 0x7ffd7c frame ...
[2023-11-01T08:03:12Z] kernel: NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus
[2023-11-01T08:03:12Z] kubelet: Killing container infer-runner (OOM) ... restart
```
maria-infra: kubectl logs for pod infer-runner-zz: stack trace shows crash in attention kernel during kv cache prefetch.
deploy-bot: deploy redwood:hotfix/quant-swap completed 20m ago by lex-eng (sha: c0ffee).
lex-eng: that deploy swapped a quantized variant for the T-Rex model to reduce memory, but there was an experimental change to prefetch logic in that build (kv prefetch window increased). rolling that back now.
oncall-juli: mitigation plan: 1) enable fallback routing for acme to cpu-compatible model variant, 2) rollback hotfix (lex), 3) reduce max in-flight context size limiter to 12k tokens for hosted pool, 4) PM to update CS with ETA. Doing 1 & 3 immediately.
tanya-runtime: log snippets look like NV driver pagefault + immediate OOM on prefetch. probable double allocation when prefetch window hits large ctx + quantized workspace bug. I want a coredump and .so offsets. Can someone grab /var/crash for the pod and upload to bucket?
maria-infra: grabbing core and heapdump now -> gs://redwood-artifacts/incidents/1698765432-infer-core.tar.gz (upload in progress). Also collecting nvml logs.
aj-support: CS update to customer: recommended temporary workaround is to set max_context=12000 on their client and reduce parallel streaming sessions. I'll send that now.
lex-eng: rollback started: `kubectl set image deployment/infer-runner infer-runner=redwood/infer-runner:stable-20231024`
Rollback should finish within 2 minutes per node. If rollback doesn't clear OOMs, we need to pin model version and increase node-level GPU memory reservation.
oncall-juli: fallback routing enabled for acme -> routed to cpu-serve variant in us-west-2. Confirming reduced 503s?
ian-cs: customer reports error rate dropped to baseline within 90s after fallback routing. They still see a few transient 503s but much better.
maria-infra: core + nvml upload complete: gs://redwood-artifacts/incidents/1698765432-infer-core.tar.gz
maria-infra: quick gdb backtrace (from core):
```
#0  0x00007f8a3b4c1a2 in attention_kernel::forward(...) at kernels/attn.cu:412
#1  0x00007f8a3b51f7c in kv_prefetch::start(...) at runtime/prefetch.cpp:88
#2  0x0000556b4a3b8c9d in runner::handle_request(...) at server/runner.cc:1021
```
tanya-runtime: repro hypothesis: 1) prefetch window scale up + quantized allocator race -> double-free/invalid pointer during memcpy, 2) leads to NV driver pagefault and OOM. We can reproduce by sending concurrent long-context prefetches against the quantized build.
lex-eng: creating a small repro harness now to flood prefetch with 4 concurrent 28k token requests. will run on a dev pool.
aj-support: CS asked whether billing might be affected for failed requests — answer: failed 503s are not billed; open a CS follow-up to reconcile any mischarged tokens.
oncall-juli: immediate action items: lex -> repro & confirm, tanya -> prepare patch for allocator safety checks, maria -> ensure rollback fully propagated and disable prefetch-window flag, aj -> customer comms. Target: stop-gap done (fallback + rollback) now, permanent patch ETA 48h.
lex-eng: repro ran: 5/5 reproduces on quant-swap image with prefetch window=2x default, 0/5 on stable image. captured ucontext and perf counters. pushing PR with minimal allocator guard.
maria-infra: rolling node-level gpu-mem-reserve to 1GB reserved for system/driver on us-west-2 pool to reduce OOM blast radius (patch applied).
ian-cs: customer confirms they've resumed normal traffic and we'll patch them in when fix merged. Thanks team.
tanya-runtime: next steps: code PR (allocator guard) -> CI gpu-run -> canary in prod with small % -> monitor nvml resets and OOMs for 24h. add a regression test in stress harness for concurrent prefetch.
aj-support: I'll send CS postmortem draft and attach repro steps so they can opt-in to canary when ready.
oncall-juli: closing incident channel once patch is validated. tagging followups: #eng-runtime for PR review, #eng-infra for pool reservation follow-ups.
deploy-bot: revert finished — stable image rolled across nodes (rollout complete).
